video_title: If Not Now, Then When Will These AI Companies Go Public?
gist: Dan Nathan and Guy Adami argue the OpenAI revenue-recognition flap (a ~$70B 'annual run rate' vs. FT-reported ~$50B) and the pulled Nscale neocloud IPO are early cracks in the debt-financed AI buildout, with private-credit lenders (Blackstone, Apollo, Blue Owl) as the canary and a Q1 2027 reckoning flagged. They also flag a 10-year stuck near 5.25-5.33% (~60bp higher since Bessent's 'I'm the house' challenge), $91 crude on the Iran war, a weak Apple setup on reported 15-20% iPhone 18 order cuts, and low-expectation but delinquency-exposed bank earnings into the midterms.

themes.theme: OpenAI revenue optics & AI IPO window

insights.claim: An FT report that OpenAI's year-end revenue would be ~$50B rather than the ~$70B the street expected, followed by the company clarifying that $70B is an annual run rate with some revenue effectively 'stuck' with customers, dropped the NASDAQ about 1.5% in a straight line on Thursday.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: AI-complex equities are hypersensitive to OpenAI financial disclosures; private-company revenue optics now move public indices.

insights.claim: Guy Adami views OpenAI, a roughly five-year-old commercial company, already using what he calls 'fugazy accounting' on revenue as a major red flag given it hemorrhages money and sits at the epicenter of the AI trade.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Revenue-quality skepticism should be priced into OpenAI's IPO and its counterparties.
insights.quote: when you're already doing fugazy accounting things at this point in the game

insights.claim: OpenAI is expected to IPO sometime in the first half of 2027 (Q1-Q2), and has been selectively leaking financials because it is still raising money in private markets.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Disclosure-driven volatility around OpenAI will likely persist until an S-1 standardizes its numbers.

insights.claim: After the OpenAI news, Oracle bounced about 5% on Friday while CoreWeave, down ~7.5% Thursday, was barely up 1%, showing neoclouds are not getting the rebound that hyperscale-adjacent names get.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Neoclouds are the weakest link in the AI chain; relative weakness vs. Oracle is a tell on credit-dependent business models.

insights.claim: Neocloud Nscale, in which Nvidia is a big investor, pulled its IPO about a week earlier despite the S&P and NASDAQ sitting at all-time highs on AI enthusiasm, which Nathan reads as a warning sign: if AI IPOs can't get done now, when can they?
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: A shut IPO window at index highs signals private-market marks and demand for AI infrastructure equity are weaker than headline indices imply.
insights.quote: How the hell can you not bring an IPO in this environment?

insights.claim: Earnings growth in the market this year is concentrated in a few names, chiefly Nvidia and Micron, so the entire stock market hinges on the success of a handful of AI companies.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Concentration means any AI-demand disappointment transmits directly to index-level earnings.

insights.claim: A delayed IPO calendar should take some premium out of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, whose investment-banking fee outlook depends on AI-era listings.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Pulled AI IPOs are a second-order headwind for capital-markets-heavy banks.

insights.claim: Blackstone, Apollo and Blue Owl bounced roughly 50-75% from their spring lows but have given back almost the entire bounce; Blackstone trades around $113 versus a low near $106 in late March/early April.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Alternative-asset managers are trading as a leveraged proxy on AI financing risk.

insights.claim: Private-credit firms are the go-to financiers for GPU (and Google TPU) purchases, raising tens of billions collateralized by GPUs, making them the 'canary in the coal mine' for the AI buildout.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Watch alt-manager stocks and GPU-backed credit spreads as the leading indicator for AI capex stress.
insights.quote: this is so obviously a canary in the coal mine. I mean, they're helping to raise tens and tens of billions of dollars collateralized by GPUs

insights.claim: Thursday's knee-jerk sell-off on the OpenAI news is a precursor to a reckoning in Q1 2027 over how much debt has been accrued by data-center builders versus actual demand.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Positions a dated window (Q1 2027) for AI-credit stress; consider hedges into that period.
insights.quote: I think is a precursor um to what we're going to see in Q1 of 2027

insights.claim: This week Oracle and Broadcom went to Apollo and Blackstone seeking ~$50B to help OpenAI make custom chips, and SpaceX is raising ~$40B, putting vendor/customer-financed AI debt raises near $100B.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Vendor financing of a cash-burning customer is circular; it amplifies counterparty risk if OpenAI demand disappoints.
insights.quote: those are the customers raing raising the debt to give them the product

insights.claim: Nathan expects the debt-funded AI buildout to eventually 'go pear-shaped' but not imminently, implying the trade can keep running in the meantime.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Timing caveat: bearish structurally, not calling an immediate top.
insights.quote: at some point, this is all going to go pear-shaped, but not in the meantime

insights.claim: The 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.24% after hitting 5.33%, with DXY near 102.5, VIX unable to reach 16, and crude around $91.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Benchmark macro levels for the setup: high rates, firm dollar, complacent equity vol, elevated oil.

insights.claim: Since Treasury Secretary Bessent said 'I'm the house' and challenged the market roughly six weeks ago, 10-year yields have risen about 60 basis points, the opposite of the administration's explicit goal of targeting lower 10-year yields.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Administration jawboning has failed; policy credibility on rates is weak.

insights.claim: Nearly every policy action since the inauguration, starting with tariffs, has pushed the 10-year yield higher despite the administration stating it was targeting that yield; 30-year mortgages recently topped out near 7.5%.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Housing affordability is worsening into the midterms, raising political pressure for any lever that lowers yields.

insights.claim: Only two things can bring yields down: ending the Iran war (crude falls knee-jerk, bonds follow) or a swift equity downturn triggering a flight to quality; the administration would prefer the first but might tolerate the second.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Implies a market sell-off is not something Washington will rush to stop; the Fed is not the lever.

insights.claim: Cool inflation prints have been met with higher bond yields, suggesting the rate problem is a global debt/deficit issue rather than just inflation.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Don't expect benign CPI/PPI alone to rally bonds; term premium and supply drive yields.
insights.quote: This is a debt problem globally

insights.claim: Nathan doubts US Treasuries would get a durable flight-to-quality bid in a sell-off because hedge funds (a concentrated buyer) and foreigners focused on deficits may not want them; Adami calls it 'perceived' quality.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Bond-equity hedge may fail; diversify hedges beyond duration.

insights.claim: CME FedWatch odds of an October 28 rate hike swung from about 70% to roughly 25%, and the hosts never expected a hike, mainly for political reasons ahead of the midterms.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Hike risk is fading; next week's CPI is the swing factor.

insights.claim: Trump's statement that the US will not attack Iran before the midterms gives away leverage; Iran and proxies are hitting US allies (a missile on a Saudi civilian airport killing three, a strike on Qatar, Houthi launches), sustaining an oil risk premium.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Expect a persistent geopolitical premium in crude while US posture is passive.
insights.quote: you are going to see a premium in oil

insights.claim: A minority view holds the Iran conflict could escalate after the midterms rather than calm down, because the administration no longer answers to voters.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Tail risk of post-election oil spike runs against consensus 'peace after midterms' expectation.
insights.quote: post election is when things actually ramp up and get worse

insights.claim: Refiners and majors (Valero, Marathon Petroleum, PSX, Chevron, Exxon) and the XLE are near all-time highs, and energy's sub-4% S&P weight could double if the AI trade unravels and capital rotates.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Energy is the natural rotation destination if AI unwinds; overweight energy as an AI hedge.
insights.quote: the energy space, which I believe is less than 4% of the S&P 500, could that double from here

insights.claim: Nikkei reports Apple cut iPhone 18/18 Pro component orders by 15-20%, knocking the stock ~2% after a period of strong relative strength driven by its lack of AI capex spending.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: The 'low-capex AI winner' narrative is vulnerable to hardware demand disappointment.

insights.claim: Apple's prior report gave weak guidance and the stock gapped down 8% the next day from all-time highs; combined with order cuts, the upcoming quarter (the new CEO's first solo call) risks soft guidance.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Earnings risk skewed negative; investors have short memories on the last guide.

insights.claim: Apple is about to test the third point of an uptrend line from spring-2026 lows near $250; a break, which Adami thinks fairly likely, could see a back-and-fill to $275, the June low.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Technical downside target of $275 on a trendline break; not the time to pile in.

insights.claim: Apple no longer drives the broader market, and the Mag 7 in general matter less to index direction than they once did.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Apple weakness alone is not an index-level risk signal.

insights.claim: Nathan expects Apple's 'Duo' product to be a big bust in the near term.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Don't underwrite new-device upside into Apple estimates.

insights.claim: Bank stocks have sold off roughly 10%; JPMorgan fell from an August all-time high near $366.50 to about $330, and the group never confirmed the S&P's new highs, partly on fears about AI's impact on bank earnings.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Low expectations into earnings; relative weakness is a breadth warning.

insights.claim: The pre-earnings bank setup looks good after the sell-off, but there is a decent chance investors pile in and are disappointed by cautious CEO commentary.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Trade the commentary, not the setup; beware crowded pre-earnings longs.

insights.claim: Below the surface the US consumer is still spending but delinquency rates are concerning, and a credit event triggered by higher yields would hurt banks.
insights.speaker: Guy Adami
insights.so_what: Rising yields plus delinquencies are the key bank risk channel to monitor in this week's reports.

insights.claim: An FT article estimated AI agents could cost banks $500B by shopping savers into better deposit rates, though banks may also gain hundreds of billions in AI cost savings.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: AI-driven deposit-rate competition is a new structural NIM risk narrative for banks.
insights.quote: AI agents could cost banks $500 billion by winning savers better rates

insights.claim: Despite stocks at all-time highs and VIX near 15, the administration lacks clarity on how markets will react to its policies, and the hosts expect equity and rate volatility into and out of the midterms; bond and single-stock volatility are already elevated, making broader volatility inevitable.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan
insights.so_what: Cheap index vol into the midterms looks mispriced given already-elevated bond and single-stock vol.
insights.quote: I think there's an inevitability to seeing a broader market uh round of volatility as well
